title: Origins · the wildcat and its cousins
blurb: Every domestic cat descends from the African wildcat; the species beside it show what the family looks like without a fireside.

items.d: The ancestor of the house cat: a sandy tabby of Africa and the Middle East, still happy to live alone.
The stocky forest cat of Europe, with a bushy ringed tail and a refusal to be tamed.
The steppe cat from the Caspian to India, spotted rather than striped and built for dry country.
A small desert hunter with furry paws and huge ears, surviving where almost no water falls.
The long-legged reed cat of South Asia, once kept for hunting waterfowl.
A rare grey cat of the Tibetan plateau, known to science for little more than a century.
One of the smallest cats, 1–2 kg, and one of the most effective hunters in southern Africa.
The manul of Central Asia: flat-faced, thick-coated and permanently unimpressed.
